title: Mobile internet access is expanding for women in LMICs, but affordability, skills, and safety preserve a large gendered usage gap
source_unit: GSMA Mobile Gender Gap Report 2026, based on GSMA Consumer Survey 2025 and modelling
geography: Low- and middle-income countries; regional estimates for Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, East Asia and Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe and Central Asia, and Latin America and Caribbean

observations.period: 2017 and 2025; LMIC women and men aged 18 and over

denominator.unit: Modelled LMIC adult population; report combines face-to-face survey results from 14 LMICs with extrapolation to other LMICs

women_mobile_internet_penetration_2025.unit: percent of women using mobile internet

gender_gap_mobile_internet.unit: percent by which women are less likely than men to use mobile internet

women_fewer_than_men.unit: million fewer women than men using mobile internet

women_not_using_mobile_internet.unit: million women in LMICs not using mobile internet

ownership_gap.unit: percent gender gap in overall mobile ownership in 2025

mechanism.value: Digital participation can expand in aggregate while gendered access gaps preserve unequal reach to information, commerce, work, services, and cultural discovery

observations.method: GSMA combines more than 16,000 face-to-face surveys across 14 LMICs with modelling and extrapolation for countries not directly surveyed; the report is an industry-sponsored research product.
observations.uncertainty: Modelled regional and LMIC estimates depend on survey coverage, self-report, sampling, extrapolation, definitions of mobile internet use, and assumptions for countries not directly surveyed. Access does not establish effective use, quality, affordability, safety, or downstream outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Women and men aged 18 and over in LMICs, with regional and country comparisons; gender is treated as a binary comparison in the published headline indicators.
observations.counterinterpretation: A narrowing aggregate gender gap can coexist with persistent country, class, age, disability, or rural gaps. More users do not imply equal capability, privacy, safety, economic benefit, or cultural agency.

observations.period: 2025; regional mobile-internet use among women and gender gaps

denominator.unit: Regional LMIC adult estimates from GSMA survey and modelling; no common person-level denominator published on the summary page

women_mobile_internet_by_region.value: 35% Sub-Saharan Africa; 51% South Asia; 87% East Asia and Pacific; 56% Middle East and North Africa; 79% Europe and Central Asia; 77% Latin America and Caribbean
women_mobile_internet_by_region.unit: percent of women using mobile internet

gender_gap_by_region.value: 26% Sub-Saharan Africa; 25% South Asia; 4% East Asia and Pacific; 15% Middle East and North Africa; 3% Europe and Central Asia; 1% Latin America and Caribbean
gender_gap_by_region.unit: percent gender gap in mobile internet use

barriers.value: affordability, digital skills, awareness, and safety or security concerns remain important barriers to adoption and use

mechanism.value: Coverage alone does not equal participation: handset cost, skills, awareness, and safety shape who can convert network availability into routine digital use

observations.method: Descriptive regional comparison from the 2026 GSMA Mobile Gender Gap summary and associated methodology materials.
observations.uncertainty: Regional figures are modelled and may conceal large within-region differences. The summary does not provide a single comparable measure of data prices, handset quality, safety incidents, or use-case completion across regions.
observations.subgroup: Women and men in LMIC regional groupings; the published summary does not provide full intersections by income, disability, age, rurality, or ethnicity.
observations.counterinterpretation: High mobile-internet penetration in a region may still mean shallow, shared, expensive, or insecure use; low gender gaps do not prove equal autonomy or benefit.

related_sources.claim: GSMA methodology for Consumer Survey 2025, modelling, extrapolation, and barrier analysis.
GSMA State of Mobile Internet Connectivity 2026 context for the global usage gap.

boundary: This record adds an LMIC digital-access and gender layer to the platform and infrastructure themes. It does not establish internet quality, financial or cultural outcomes, platform causation, safety incidence, household welfare, or equal effective agency.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: GSMA Mobile Gender Gap 2026 official summary page reviewed for global and regional mobile-internet penetration, gender gaps, user counts, barrier categories, survey scope, and modelling caveats.
